intro: East Hollywood takes in Thai Town, Little Armenia, Virgil Village and the Melrose Hill strip, between Hollywood and Los Feliz. It is one of the deepest eating neighborhoods in LA, with some of the city's best Thai cooking, a run of chef-driven spots on Melrose and a few great small bars.

gm: Google Maps reviews (local favorites we checked)

places.w: Crackly, deeply browned bagels that draw a morning line and can sell out.
places.o: The burnt everything bagel with salmon. Go before 10am.

places.w: A roomy neighborhood cafe in a converted industrial space, with a calm back area for working.
places.o: A shaken espresso.

places.w: Despite the name, a no-frills Thai noodle shop that ranks among the best Thai restaurants in LA.
places.o: Boat noodle soup and the jade noodles.

places.w: A Thai noodle shop built around glazed roast duck.
places.o: The duck special with garlicky jade noodles.

places.w: A focused Thai counter for Hainan-style chicken rice.
places.o: Chicken rice plus the crispy zaab chicken to share.

places.w: A tiny Northern Thai spot in a strip mall, great for a solo lunch.
places.o: Khao soi and the sai oua sausage.

places.w: Big Italian-American subs and breakfast sandwiches.
places.o: Meatball parm or the chicken cutlet with vodka sauce.

places.w: A Filipino grill whose big trays are built for sharing with a group.
places.o: A tapsilog tray or the lucenachon rice bowl.

places.w: A fast-casual Caribbean counter with big flavors.
places.o: Goat roti, plantains and the curry mac and cheese.

places.w: A small seafood cafe: sandwiches by day, a more ambitious menu at night.
places.o: A tuna melt at lunch or scallop crudo at dinner.

places.w: A Thai Town institution known for fiery Southern Thai cooking.
places.o: The crispy catfish salad and stir-fried garlic crab.

places.w: A late-night Thai Town standby that is best for stir-fries.
places.o: Crispy catfish with basil.

places.w: Oaxacan cooking anchored by a smoky goat birria.
places.o: The oversized goat birria taco and a tlayuda to share.

places.w: A family-run Lebanese and Armenian restaurant in Little Armenia.
places.o: A spread of mezze including muhammara and sujuk.

places.w: A wood-fired Middle Eastern kebab house from the team behind Bavel and Bestia.
places.o: Hummus, then a big kebab platter for the table.

places.w: A small, buzzing raw bar with excellent oysters.
places.o: Oysters, the crab dip and the big seafood platter.

places.w: A candlelit Italian room with a focus on grilled meats.
places.o: The salt-and-pepper New York strip.

places.w: Rotating dinners cooked by refugee and immigrant chefs, often with live jazz.
places.o: Check the schedule and go for a themed dinner night.

places.w: A lively izakaya with shochu cocktails and shareable plates.
places.o: Thai sausage and the wagyu yakisoba.

places.w: A cozy French wine bar with a short, satisfying menu.
places.o: Steak frites and the gruyere tart.

places.w: A stylish little cocktail bar in Virgil Village with a smoking patio.
places.o: A house cocktail; Mondays bring a tiki menu.
